properties.description: The subclassification relationships owned here that identify this classifier as the more specific classifier.
The ordered features whose successive navigation determines this feature’s modeled values.
The navigational feature constraining collections reached across the other ends of the same owning type.
Describes whether modeled feature values serve as inputs, outputs, or both.
The type owning this feature through an end-feature membership.
The final feature in this feature’s navigation chain, or this feature when no chain exists.
The types that every domain instance from which this feature is evaluated must satisfy.
Makes modeled values dependent on their featuring instance for continued existence and exclusive to that instance across composite features.
Keeps the modeled value unchanged across snapshots even when the feature is variable.
Indicates that modeled values of this feature are always computable from other feature values.
Marks a feature as an end, mapping each domain instance to one value; navigation cardinality can additionally be constrained through its cross feature.
Records whether the modeled feature values have a meaningful sequence.
Indicates that modeled values are spatial or temporal portions of their domain instance and represent that same thing.
Requires the modeled collection of feature values to contain no repeated values when true.
Allows the modeled feature value to differ between snapshots of an occurrence owning type.
The optional owned cross-subsetting relationship specifying this feature’s cross-navigation constraint.
The owned relationships specifying the ordered steps used to navigate this feature.
The owned relationships that give this feature an inverse navigation interpretation.
The owned subsetting relationships that replace inherited features with this redefining feature.
The optional owned reference-subsetting relationship identifying the feature referenced by this feature.
The owned specializations that constrain this feature to select values from another feature.
The owned type-featuring relationships that explicitly identify contexts featuring this feature.
The owned feature-typing relationships that constrain the types of this feature’s modeled values.
The membership that owns this feature as a feature of its owning type.
The type that owns this feature through its owning feature membership.
The types that every modeled value of this feature must satisfy, including types obtained through specialization and chaining.
The ordered types defining this type as the first type’s interpretations minus those of subsequent types.
The features of this type with an explicit direction.
The features of this type marked as ends.
The features available through this type’s feature memberships, including inherited features.
The owned and inherited feature memberships of this type, excluding imported memberships.
The features obtained through inherited feature memberships.
The memberships made available to this type by specialization or conjugation.
The features of this type directed into the type, including bidirectional features.
The types whose shared interpretations define this type.
Requires every instance of this type to also instantiate a more specialized type.
Records whether this type owns a conjugation as its conjugator.
Makes satisfying this type’s classification conditions sufficient for classification by the type.
The owned multiplicity constraining this type’s modeled cardinality; without one, applicable supertype multiplicities still constrain it.
The features of this type directed out of the type, including bidirectional features.
The optional conjugation owned here that treats this type as the original type.
The owned difference relationships defining this type as their difference result.
The owned disjointness relationships constraining this type against other types.
The end features introduced through memberships owned by this type.
The features introduced through feature memberships owned by this type.
The memberships owned here that introduce owned features of this type.
The owned intersection relationships defining this type as their intersection result.
The owned specialization relationships in which this type is the more specific type.
The owned union relationships defining this type as their union result.
The types whose combined interpretations equal this type’s interpretation.
The associations that classify the links identified by this connector.
The connector’s end features, which redefine association ends and reference the connected features.
The innermost shared featuring context of the related features that would satisfy the connector’s type-featuring check, if one exists.
The features connected by this connector, obtained from the features referenced by its ends.
The first related feature, treated as the connector’s source.
The related features after the first, treated as the connector’s targets.
Alternative identifiers for this element, typically supplied by tools.
The primary name explicitly supplied for this element.
An explicitly supplied compact alternative name whose contextual uniqueness is the modeler’s responsibility.
The documentation elements owned by this element.
The tooling-assigned global identifier intended to remain stable for this element’s lifetime.
Records that all required implied owned relationships are included; false requires that none be included.
Indicates that this element lies within the ownership tree of a library model.
The effective name used for namespace lookup, which some element kinds compute rather than declare.
The annotation relationships owned here that annotate this element.
The elements reached as owned related elements through this element’s owned relationships.
The relationships owned by this element as their owning related element.
The owning related element reached through this element’s owning relationship, which need not be a namespace.
The relationship owning this element when that relationship is a membership.
The namespace obtained through this element’s owning membership, when that ownership route exists.
The relationship that directly owns this element as a related element, if one exists.
The ownership-path name in KerML syntax, absent when the named ownership path or disambiguation conditions are not met.
The effective compact name used for namespace lookup, which some element kinds compute rather than declare.
The textual-representation annotations attached to this element.
Identifies a relationship introduced by tooling to satisfy language semantics rather than directly authored by a modeler.
The participating elements directly owned by this relationship.
The participating element that owns this relationship, if present.
The elements participating in the relationship, collected from its sources and targets.
The participating elements treated as the relationship’s origins.
The participating elements treated as the relationship’s destinations.
The memberships made available by imports owned by this namespace.
The elements available as members through this namespace’s memberships.
The memberships available in this namespace, including owned and imported memberships.
The import relationships owned by this namespace.
The member elements owned through this namespace’s owned memberships.
The memberships owned by this namespace.
